records.note: A board complaint 'waiting to happen' names no board, no clinician and no complaint. The registry holds no medical-board discipline event. No criterion can be written.
'The only fun that matters' with 'a somber, defensible go-to-market strategy' is a slogan. No company, no market outcome and no threshold; nothing in the registry matches.
Blackberry and iPhone are an analogy, not a benchmark. 'Only to fail' names no company, no market event and no date. Comparative with no measurable benchmark.

'Has promise in suicidal patients' characterizes present evidence. It names no trial, no endpoint and no readout, so no trial_result item can be written. E-0006 and E-0060 need a named trial and a primary result; the words give neither.
A legal characterization of plan sponsors, not a payer action. No named payer, no coverage policy and no lawsuit. 'Going forward' is not a deadline. E-0046 needs a filed suit; none is predicted.

The subject is the author's own newsletter going viral. That is not a drug, device or treatment decision, trial result, company or market outcome, payer decision, or practice adoption. Area test fails first.

'Might call an extravagant claim' predicts an FDA opinion, not an action. No untitled letter, warning letter or enforcement step is asserted, and the registry holds no FDA promotion-enforcement event.
'We get more' regulation is a direction with no countable set, no named rule and no series. No rule_or_policy item can be written from the words.
'Employers will call their benefits broker' names no employer, no broker and no observable record. The suit clause states an interest, not a filing. No registry event matches.
'They' is employers in general, with no countable set and no named plan or payer. 'A compliant plan' has no criterion. The enrollment cycle gives no date the words fix.
'Applied for damages under ADA next' names no court, no case and no party. Perez v. Sturgis is the cited precedent, not the predicted docket. No court_outcome item can be written.
'Trial design will need to embrace the most robust safety standards' names no sponsor, no trial and no FDA action. 'The most robust' has no threshold.
A comparative on staffing difficulty with no benchmark and no data series. Nothing observable resolves 'more challenging to staff'.
'Some breaks will need to be taken' states a staffing consequence, not an event a third party decides. No sponsor, trial or criterion.
'Clarification will be required' names no FDA document, no guidance finalization and no date. 'Paramount concerns' has no criterion. The registry holds no psychedelic-guidance finalization event.
The claim is about the appeal of Doblin's motives and messaging. It is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome.
'The more therapists exposed, the fewer will have doubt' gives no countable set and no measure of doubt. 'Some of the time, they will not help' has no trial, endpoint or threshold.
'Psychedelic exceptionalism' is a slogan, and 'get in the way of psychedelic medicine being actual medicine' has no observable criterion. The first clause is normative.
'Other people' and 'your interventions' name no gatekeeper, no body and no intervention. 'Don't go anywhere' has no criterion.
'Till the FDA takes it down' names no company, no promotional piece and no enforcement document. The registry holds no FDA promotion-enforcement event, so nothing can be matched or written.
'Private equity cannot generate value' names no fund, no company and no metric. American Physician Partners is the cited example, not the subject of a predicted event.
The claim depends on a personal-liability rule the author proposes and that does not exist. 'Deterring them from meddling' has no countable set or threshold.

'California will dictate the standards' names no bill, rule or agency action, and 'all healthcare products' has no countable set. It is also conditional on HIPAA being scrapped, which is not asserted as a fact.
'Take a swing at Texas in this manner' names no bill, no rule and no enforcement step. Nothing observable resolves it.
'Privacy is over' and 'privacy is a terrible legal framework' are present-tense judgements of a legal framework. No future state is asserted, so the expectation test fails.
'50% never do each year, and climbing' names no data series, no threshold and no period end. A quantity_threshold item needs a named series; the registry holds no deductible series.
'Big Insurance' is not a countable set of companies and no named revenue series is given. The $1.38 trillion figure is the distance to Saturn in meters used as a joke, not a stated revenue threshold.
'Big Health can not stop putting the squeeze on you' is a slogan. No company, metric or threshold; 'we can never get there' has no criterion for 'value'.
'Can't be undone by outsiders' and 'too powerful' name no company, no event and no measure. Nothing observable resolves it.
'Taken down by those who ran the scam' names no company and no observable event, and 'Big Health Mafia' is not a countable set. No date.
'The answer is likely to surprise you' gives no price, no threshold and no drug. No quantity or coverage item can be written.
'Others will sue and win' names no plaintiff, defendant, court or claim. E-0046 is a different asset (a parity pleading) and a different outcome type (filed, not won), so it is not a match.
'Vastly reducing the cost of the litigation' has no cost figure, no filing and no docket event. A litigation-process expectation with no observable criterion.
'Payers demand pilots that will fail' is an aphorism. No payer, no pilot and no countable set; 'fail' has no criterion.
'No healthcare play can succeed' names no company and gives no success criterion or countable set. An aphoristic rule, not an event.
A generic claim about venture-backed healthcare startups. No company, no quality measure and no threshold.
'A business that fails the second the cash dries up' names no company and no date. A truism about burn rate, with no countable set.
'May lead to less abuse of others' names no trial, no series and no threshold. Treating NPD is not tied to any observable adoption or outcome measure.
'Every employer' has no countable set, and the disjunction (sue or carry liability) cannot be falsified. No named plan, suit or parity pleading, so E-0046 does not fit.

The consequent, 'every lawyer everywhere is going to bring the same claim', has no countable set and no criterion. The condition, 'one of these lawsuits wins', names no case and is not the filing event E-0046 holds.
